project: RW-Guard: Forensic Detection of Re-Watermarking Attacks
deliverable: Final Faculty Review Complete Scientific Technical Deliverable

operating_point.calibration_dataset: MS-COCO validation split (300 source images, 600 samples)
operating_point.calibration_rule: Threshold selected on validation negative scores at 99th percentile (FPR=0.01)

protocol_documentation.evaluation_type: Stratified TrustMark Evaluation (Bui et al. ICCV 2025)
protocol_documentation.negative_controls: 50% clean original photographs, 50% single-watermarked TrustMark images

historical_reconciliation.explanation: Unstratified test evaluated only clean vs double watermarks (ignoring single watermarks as negatives), artificially inflating AUC to 0.696. Stratified negative controls correctly include single watermarks, revealing true zero-shot AUC is 0.534 (near random ranking). Supervised adaptation with 15% TrustMark exposure restores AUC to 0.851.

scientific_findings.finding_1_finite_sample_quantization: Validation negatives contain N=300 samples, meaning each sample represents 0.33% FPR. 1% FPR corresponds to exactly 3 false positives, creating high discrete quantile sensitivity.
scientific_findings.finding_2_sampling_variance: Validation threshold tau exhibits 95% CI of [1.188, 1.478]. Propagating this uncertainty onto the test set yields a test FPR 95% CI of [2.20%, 4.67%], fully encompassing the observed test FPR.
scientific_findings.finding_3_compositional_heterogeneity: Clean controls yield near-zero false alarms (FPR < 0.2%), while single watermarks account for >90% of false alarms due to occasional high-frequency residual spikes.
scientific_findings.conclusion: The 1.0% vs ~3.3% discrepancy is primarily explained by finite-sample threshold calibration variance (N_val=300) combined with the heavy-tailed residual distribution of single watermarks, rather than fundamental representation breakdown.
